description: TrashNet is the waste-image dataset collected by Gary Thung and Mindy Yang and published with their classification project. The repository documents 2,527 images in six classes: glass, paper, cardboard, plastic, metal and other trash. Objects were photographed on white posterboard with several iPhone models under sunlight or indoor lighting, with a resized 512 by 384 pixel version. Coverage is object-level and experimental, not a geographic waste survey; dates and collection representativeness are not specified. The authors link their public Hugging Face dataset, which states MIT terms, alongside the MIT repository. A limitation is the controlled background and imbalanced classes, especially the 137-image residual-trash category. The hosted viewer reports 5,054 rows, which is not treated as proof of that many independent original objects. The dataset can calibrate classification components for waste-sorting simulations, complementing SwolfPy (model-swolfpy). The student training exercise is not the proposed resource: the separately published and documented dataset is reusable under the user's inclusion rule. No images, model weights or course report PDF were downloaded.
